learning_outcomes.text: Students can explain, understand, calculate, and evaluate the basic technical contexts, development goals, and functionalities of motor vehicles (cars, trucks) and their components. The focus is on vehicle vertical and lateral dynamics.
Students know basic model approaches for describing the vertical and lateral dynamic vibration characteristics of vehicles and can calculate all essential driving state variables.
Students are familiar with the components of the chassis and can calculate and design them with regard to driving dynamics requirements.
Students understand the driver's tasks in the driver-vehicle-environment control loop and can analyze the interactions of longitudinal, lateral, and vertical dynamics.

syllabus_topics: Suspension components of the vehicle and their requirements
Vertical dynamic modeling (quarter-vehicle, single-track, and two-track suspension models)
Requirements and properties of tires regarding lateral and vertical dynamics
Analysis of lateral dynamic driving behavior and objective setting using different model approaches (single-track, two-track, and full-vehicle models)
Kinematics and elastokinematics of wheel suspensions and their effects on driving dynamics
Steering systems and implemented chassis systems
Chassis tuning and assessment of driving behavior
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam and the laboratory practical (study achievement). The grade's weight for the final grade is determined by credit points.
